clue.text: Fight fire in Bergen?

blocks.note: a ruck is a scrum or brawl
to fire someone is to sack them

explanation.surface: A call to put out a blaze in the Norwegian port of Bergen.
explanation.walkthrough: Bergen looks like the Norwegian city, but a bergen is also a large military backpack, named after a Norwegian design; the question mark flags the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A bergen is a type of large rucksack carried by soldiers, so the word is an example of the answer.

clue.text: Portion of mackerel - is hollandaise sauce required?

indicators.note: a portion is a part taken from a larger whole, so the letters are lifted from the words that follow

blocks.note: the run of letters spans three words

explanation.surface: A diner asks whether hollandaise is needed with a serving of mackerel.
explanation.walkthrough: Hollandaise sauce reads as one phrase, but the hidden run stops inside hollandaise and 'sauce' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A relish is a tangy condiment or sauce served with food.

clue.text: Protect famous clown willing to participate

blocks.note: Coco was a celebrated circus clown with the Bertram Mills Circus
someone up for it is 'on', as in 'are you on?'

explanation.surface: Shielding a well-known clown who is keen to join in.
explanation.definitionFit: To cocoon someone is to wrap them up safely, as a silkworm is enclosed.

clue.text: Take whisky, for example, before good savoury item

blocks.note: Scotch is whisky made in Scotland
e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for example
G is the standard abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Have a whisky before tucking into a decent savoury snack.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scotch egg is a hard-boiled egg wrapped in sausage meat and breadcrumbs, a British picnic snack.

clue.text: In a magazine, a cocktail for a man of the world

blocks.note: first meanings: the women's glossy magazine of that title, and the vodka and cranberry cocktail
last meaning: a worldly, widely travelled person

explanation.walkthrough: The clue actually gives three meanings: a magazine, a cocktail and a worldly person.
explanation.definitionFit: A cosmopolitan is someone at home in many countries and cultures, as well as the magazine title and the drink.

clue.text: Briefly visit doctor, at home after work

indicators.note: after places the words before it later in the answer, so the home piece follows the work piece

blocks.note: DR is the usual abbreviation for doctor
an op, short for opus, is a musical work
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: A GP calls round for a short home visit once the working day is over.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads 'at home after work' but the pieces run doctor, work, then at home.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop in is to call on someone casually for a short time.

clue.text: Step right up and one may get run over

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading the letters from bottom to top

blocks.note: a pace is a single step
R abbreviates right

explanation.surface: A fairground barker's call to step right up, though someone might get hit by a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Step right up' reads as an invitation, and 'run over' as a road accident; it means to summarise.
explanation.definitionFit: To recap is to go back over the main points, so it is a synonym for running over something.

clue.text: Make a public announcement in favour of demand

blocks.note: pro means for or in favour of
to claim is to demand as a right

explanation.surface: Speaking out publicly in support of a demand.
explanation.definitionFit: To proclaim is to declare something officially and openly.

clue.text: Gets gen off about Society and savings

indicators.note: off means gone bad or out of order, so the letters are rearranged
about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the next piece

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
S abbreviates society

explanation.surface: Someone gets information from a building society about their savings.
explanation.walkthrough: Gen is British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: A nest egg is money put aside for the future, so the plural means savings.

clue.text: 10 intercepted by the French in game

indicators.note: an intercepted pass is caught between players, so one item sits between the letters of another

blocks.note: le is French for 'the'
the answer to 10 across

explanation.surface: A pass intercepted by the French team during a match.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference '10' imports the answer to 10 across; it sits between the two letters of the French article.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacrosse is a team sport played with netted sticks, so it is an instance of a game.

clue.text: A bad-tempered over

blocks.note: taken as written
cross means angry or irritable

explanation.surface: A cricket over bowled in a foul mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' suggests cricket, but here it is the preposition: to go over a road is to go to the other side of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean on or to the other side of something, as in 'the house over the road'.

clue.text: Deed Ghandi forged with an ulterior motive

indicators.note: something forged is hammered into a new shape, so these letters are reshaped

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange, with the name in this spelling
taken as written and joining the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Gandhi's deeds were faked by someone with a secret purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: The usual spelling is Gandhi; the clue's Ghandi spelling supplies the same letters, so the anagram still works.
explanation.definitionFit: A hidden agenda is a concealed aim behind someone's actions, which is what an ulterior motive is.

clue.text: Impassive, one cutting incomplete pile of cards after a deal

indicators.note: something incomplete is missing its final part, so the last letter goes
a thing cutting through another goes into its middle

blocks.clueFragment: pile of cards after a deal
blocks.note: in card games the stock is the undealt pile left after the deal
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A poker-faced player cuts the deck after the cards are dealt.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping its last letter from the card pile gives STOC, and the numeral cuts in before its final C.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoic person endures hardship without showing feeling, so the adjective means unmoved or impassive.

clue.text: Without thinking, I slump lazily in one

indicators.note: done lazily, the letters are left lying in a careless jumble
these letters are placed inside another word

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone flops lazily into a chair without a thought.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting on impulse means acting spontaneously, with no forethought.

clue.text: Substitute in back row

blocks.note: to second a motion is to back or support it
a string is a line or row of things

explanation.surface: A replacement player put into the back row of a rugby scrum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back row' looks like a rugby position but splits into two separate verbs and nouns.
explanation.definitionFit: A second-string player is a reserve, kept to stand in for the first choice.

clue.text: Little time to request Church of England to form a working party

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
to ask for something is to request it
CE abbreviates the Church of England

explanation.surface: Short of time, the Church of England is asked to set up a committee.
explanation.definitionFit: A task force is a group formed for a specific job, much like a working party appointed to study an issue.

clue.text: Trouble concealing blemish? Just the opposite with cosmetics

indicators.note: concealing means hiding inside; 'just the opposite' swaps which piece hides which

blocks.note: a wart is a small growth that blemishes skin
a pain is a nuisance or trouble

explanation.surface: Make-up used to hide a skin blemish, or perhaps the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, trouble would hide the blemish; 'Just the opposite' says the blemish hides the trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: War paint is humorous slang for heavy make-up, after the face paint worn before battle.

clue.text: Demote king's English envoy

blocks.note: R for rex, Latin for king
E abbreviates English
a legate is an ambassador, especially of the Pope

explanation.surface: A monarch's English ambassador is moved down the ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: To relegate is to move someone or something to a lower rank or division.

clue.text: Actor offering beer (cold), and stout

blocks.note: ale is a type of beer
C for cold, as on a tap
Guinness is the best-known Irish stout

explanation.surface: A thespian standing a round of drinks: a cold beer and a stout.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Alec Guinness was the English film actor of Kind Hearts and Coronets and Star Wars.

clue.text: American hood seen in German city, and in Paris

blocks.note: Bonn was West Germany's capital city
et is French for 'and'

explanation.surface: An American car hood spotted in a German city and in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition says what Americans call a hood is, in Britain, this word for the cover over a car's engine.
explanation.definitionFit: The British bonnet of a car is the part Americans call the hood.

clue.text: Only just see under counter

indicators.note: in a down clue, under puts the piece named before it lower in the column, so it comes second

blocks.note: a bar is a counter where drinks are served
a see is a bishop's diocese, and Ely in Cambridgeshire is one

explanation.surface: Barely glimpsing something hidden under the shop counter.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'under' puts the second piece below the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Barely means scarcely or by the narrowest margin.

clue.text: The oldest service provider?

blocks.note: surface reading: a hint at the so-called oldest profession
setter's reading: the Royal Navy is the Senior Service, the oldest of the armed forces, and this group supplied it with men

explanation.walkthrough: The 'oldest profession' joke pulls towards prostitution; the real service is the navy, known as the Senior Service, which was once crewed by forcibly recruited men.
explanation.definitionFit: A press gang seized men and forced them into naval service, so it literally provided the Senior Service with crew.

clue.text: Small market, well-kept

blocks.note: S abbreviates small, as on clothing labels
a mart is a market

explanation.surface: A tidy little marketplace.
explanation.definitionFit: Smart describes something neat, tidy and well looked after.

clue.text: Girl from fine Hebridean island

blocks.note: F for fine, as on pencil leads
Iona is an island in the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland

explanation.surface: A young woman who comes from a lovely Scottish island.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiona is a girl's given name, so it is an example of a girl.

clue.text: Fashionable elsewhere, to some extent

blocks.note: what is fashionable is in
someone elsewhere is away

explanation.surface: Something is somewhat in vogue in other places.
explanation.definitionFit: 'In a way' is the idiom for partly or in some respects.

clue.text: Cast a spell on the way in

blocks.note: first meaning: to bewitch, stressed on the second syllable
second meaning: a door or gateway, stressed on the first syllable

explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are spelt the same but pronounced differently.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to put someone into a trance; the noun is the doorway by which you enter.

clue.text: Deal with Italy, ultimately establishing alliance

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very end, so only the closing letter counts

blocks.note: to treat a matter is to deal with it
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Negotiating with Italy to set up a pact.
explanation.definitionFit: A treaty is a formal agreement between states, the document behind an alliance.

clue.text: Wall hanging records experiment

blocks.note: to tape something is to record it
a try is a test or experiment

explanation.surface: A wall chart that logs the results of a trial.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapestry is a woven textile picture hung on a wall as decoration.
